Text: `var` was introduced in Java {{c1::10}} via JEP {{c2::286}}. It performs {{c3::compile-time type inference}} from the {{c4::right-hand side initializer}} and generates bytecode identical to an explicitly typed declaration.
Extra: var is NOT dynamic typing — the type is fixed at compile time and cannot change.

Text: `var` cannot be used for {{c1::fields}}, {{c2::method parameters}}, {{c3::return types}}, or {{c4::uninitialized declarations}}. These restrictions preserve type visibility at API boundaries.
Code: // var x;            // COMPILE ERROR\n// var y = null;      // COMPILE ERROR\n// class Foo { var z = 5; } // COMPILE ERROR (field)

Text: Java Records automatically generate: {{c1::private final fields}}, a {{c2::canonical constructor}}, {{c3::component accessor methods}} (no `get` prefix), {{c4::`equals()`}}, {{c5::`hashCode()`}}, and {{c6::`toString()`}}.
Extra: Records are implicitly `final` and implicitly extend `java.lang.Record`.
Code: record Point(int x, int y) {}  // generates x(), y(), equals, hashCode, toString

Text: In a Record compact constructor, the parameter list is {{c1::omitted (implied)}} and the field assignments are {{c2::auto-inserted by the compiler after the constructor body}}. You can {{c3::modify parameters}} before they are assigned to fields.
Sealed classes restrict which classes can extend them using the {{c1::`permits`}} keyword. Permitted subclasses must declare one of: {{c2::`final`}}, {{c3::`sealed`}}, or {{c4::`non-sealed`}}.
Extra: Adding `non-sealed` reopens the hierarchy; `sealed` creates a multi-level sealed hierarchy.
Code: sealed class Shape permits Circle, Square {}

Text: When a sealed class is used in a switch expression and all permitted subtypes are covered, a {{c1::`default` case is NOT required}}. The compiler {{c2::verifies exhaustiveness}} at compile time. Adding a new permitted subtype without updating the switch causes a {{c3::compile error}}.
Extra: This is the key safety advantage of sealed types over open class hierarchies.
Code: switch (shape) {\n    case Circle c -> ...\n    case Square s -> ... // exhaustive — no default needed

Text: In Pattern Matching for Switch, a {{c1::more specific (guarded) pattern}} must appear {{c2::before}} a {{c3::more general (unguarded) pattern}} of the same type. A pattern that can never be reached is {{c4::dominated}} and causes a {{c5::compile error}}.

Virtual threads were introduced in Java {{c1::21}} via JEP {{c2::444}}. They are {{c3::JVM-managed}} lightweight threads running on a small pool of {{c4::OS carrier threads}}. Blocking a virtual thread on I/O {{c5::unmounts it}} from the carrier thread.
Extra: Platform threads each require one OS thread (~1MB stack); virtual threads share carriers via mount/unmount.

Text: Virtual threads are {{c1::pinned}} to their carrier thread when blocking inside {{c2::a `synchronized` block}}. The fix is to use {{c3::ReentrantLock}} instead, which allows the JVM to {{c4::unmount}} the virtual thread from the carrier.
Extra: Java 24+ plans to fix synchronized pinning, but ReentrantLock is the current mitigation.

Text: `SequencedCollection` (Java 21) adds `{{c1::getFirst()}}`, `{{c2::getLast()}}`, `{{c3::addFirst()}}`, `{{c4::addLast()}}`, and `{{c5::reversed()}}` to all ordered collections. `reversed()` returns an {{c6::O(1) view}}, not a copy.
Switch expressions introduced in Java {{c1::14}} use the `{{c2::->}}` operator which prevents {{c3::fall-through}}. To return a value from a multi-line case block, use the `{{c4::yield}}` keyword.
Text blocks (`"""..."""`) were introduced in Java {{c1::15}}. The opening `"""` must be followed by a {{c2::newline}}. Leading whitespace is {{c3::stripped relative to the closing `"""`}} position.
Extra: The closing `"""` position determines the common indent level stripped from all lines.
